t: This is Chester House, a detached house on Clarendon Place in Tyburnia. The architect Giles Gilbert Scott designed it as his own home. He moved in when it was finished in 1926 and lived here until he died in 1960. Scott is the man behind Battersea Power Station, Liverpool Cathedral and the red telephone box. The house is built in what the listing calls a restrained, carefully proportioned stripped Renaissance style. In 1928 it won the Royal Institute of British Architects medal for London street architecture. It has been Grade II listed since 1975.
